  even when its arithmetic is correct. A first-order method, for example, shows
  gaps near 1.4e-11. If you relax 1e-14, the 0.5% limit decides whether the test
  passes. Then set that limit above the method's own gaps at steps of 0.1 s,
  0.05 s and 0.025 s, and below a difference that a learner could see. The
  constants are in `tests/reference/test_sevo_patient.py`.

[3] rewrite

```
**The release check, and why it allows 0.5%.** The model advances in fixed
steps of 0.1 s, and a shorter step should give almost the same result. Before
each release, a test reruns the first minute of the default sevoflurane
induction with steps of 0.1 s, 0.05 s and 0.025 s. Each run's alveolar,
vessel-rich and mixed-venous concentrations must be within 0.5% of the run with
the next shorter step. The 0.5% was set for the simulator's earlier calculation
method, at about ten times the 0.04% alveolar difference that method showed.
The current method's runs agree to better than one part in a trillion
(measured 2026-10-03), so the much tighter limits above are the ones that would
catch a real error. Where a compartment holds almost no agent, its values from
two runs also pass if they differ by less than 0.000001 vol%, because there a
tiny difference is a large percentage.
```

[4] rewrite

```
The 5e-3 relative tolerance was chosen when the simulator used an earlier,
approximate method (an operator split). That method gave a relative gap of 4e-4
in the alveolar fraction between steps of 0.1 s and 0.025 s, and 5e-3 is about
ten times that gap. With the current, exact method, the same comparison gives
gaps of about 1.4e-13 relative (measured 2026-10-03), so 5e-3 is kept as a
coarse check. The 1e-8 absolute tolerance lets a negligible difference pass
when the fraction is so close to zero that a relative gap means little.
```
